newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China to hold military exercise near Taiwan - report.
newsitem.headline: China to hold military exercise near Taiwan - report.

text.p: China planned to hold a joint-forces military exercise in coastal Fujian, Guangdong and Zhejiang provinces in April, the United Daily News quoted military intelligence sources as saying on Monday.
The military sources told the newspaper that they have not been able to determine whether the planned exercise was a routine drill or a politically motivated exercise aimed at intimidating Taiwan.
The planned military drill may include warning firings of guided missiles, sea and air blockade, landing exercise, or anti-missile practice, the report said.
The exact date, location and scale of the manoeuvres would be decided by Chinese communist leaders depending on relations between Taiwan and China, it said.
The military souces did not rule out the possibility that Beijing planned to use the exercise to protest at the Dalai Lama's current six-day trip in Taiwan.
Taiwan's military would monitor the situation closely, the sources added.

Beijing has assailed the Tibetan Buddhist god-king's visit -- and particularly his expected March 27 meeting with Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui -- as the collusion of "splittists" seeking independence from China for both Tibet and Nationalist-ruled Taiwan.

China held rounds of war games and missile tests near Taiwan around the island's first direct presidential election in March 1996 in what Beijing acknowledged as a bid to warn Taiwan voters not to drop a pledge to reunify with the mainland.
China, which has regarded Taiwan as renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, vows to attack the island if it opts for independence.
Last week, Taiwan's military test-fired two U.S. Hawk missiles in the Taiwan Strait, resuming live-fire manoeuvres suspended a year ago in a bid to cool acute tensions with arch rival China.
